status: Deferred — source safeguards are fixed; remaining Slice C requires an owner policy ruling on cross-card index authority. No live residue is present as of 2026-09-01.
finding: A task-scoped governed commit can successfully advance HEAD from its sealed candidate and then fail while reconciling the committed paths back into the shared live index because another Git process briefly owns .git/index.lock. The durable ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED receipt correctly preserves this non-green postcondition, but recovery still requires an operator to wait for the lock and restage paths manually.
expectedBehavior: The sealed commit and live-index reconciliation boundary must model HEAD-advanced/index-not-yet-reconciled as a durable, idempotently retryable transition. Transient index-lock contention must enqueue or retry only the irreducible reconciliation write window, preserve every foreign staged blob exactly, and release immediately after success. A successful Git commit must never be rolled back or repeated, and a reconciliation failure must never be reported as a fully clean commit result.
evidenceOrRepro: Two independent governed commits on 2026-08-12 advanced HEAD while 125 and 140 foreign staged entries remained byte-identical, then encountered .git/index.lock during live-index reconciliation. The first failure was observed at 2026-08-12T14:54:13Z and the second is preserved at .atm/history/evidence/ATM-GOV-0352.live-index-reconciliation.json with createdAt 2026-08-12T15:12:52.706Z, headAdvanced=true, clean=false, and code ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED. Commits 1b5a8e84 and e16e5894 remained valid; after the lock cleared, targeted staging restored the live index. TASK-ERR-0014 therefore proved observability and commit preservation, while the automatic retry/short-queue postcondition remains open.
followUp: Attach a successor repair card to the ATM-GOV-0351/TASK-ERR-0014 semantic family. Implement one public reconciliation operation that consumes the durable receipt, verifies the recorded HEAD and candidate lineage, waits or queues only for the short index mutation, retries idempotently, preserves concurrent foreign blob ids, and marks the receipt clean only after an independent index oracle passes. Add deterministic tests for lock held before reconciliation, lock released then retry, HEAD moved after receipt, repeated retry, and concurrent foreign index mutation. Treat candidate-scope contamination and live-surface pre-commit/record-commit analysis as related but separately testable seams; do not hard-code task IDs, path lists, entry counts, or sleep durations. 2026-08-13 amplification evidence: consecutive reconciliation failures accumulate. After six governed commits taken while one orphaned .git/index.lock persisted, the live index carried 44 staged-deletion entries for files that HEAD already contained, and pre-commit began demanding broker compose receipts for them. The boundary is now precisely measured: governed commit and governed push both run entirely through the sealed candidate index and completed normally throughout, while taskflow close cannot — it either runs git restore --worktree under --defer-foreign-state, or trips ATM_CLOSE_WINDOW_FOREIGN_STAGED_TASKS on the accumulated residue without it. So a single orphaned lock does not stop delivery, but it does stop closure, and the damage compounds with every commit taken in that state. A retry that only repairs the current commit is therefore not sufficient; the reconciliation debt itself has to be drainable. 2026-08-27 remaining scope after the contention quickfix: the retry closes the common transient case and makes the debt enumerable, but the durable drain is still not a public operation. Attach the successor repair card for (a) an operation that consumes the ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED receipt itself, verifies recorded HEAD and candidate lineage, and drains accumulated debt across several commits rather than only the current one — recoverLiveIndexAfterSuccessfulCommit already recovers a single named commit and is the natural seam to generalise; (b) the taskflow close path, which is the surface that actually breaks under accumulated residue, since governed commit and push both continue to run through the sealed candidate index; and (c) an independent index oracle that marks a receipt clean. The retry policy defaults are deliberately configurable rather than hard-coded so a successor card can tune or replace them without touching the reconciliation loop. 2026-08-28 remaining scope after the drain quickfix: (a) the 88 receipts already on disk predate lineage and are reported honestly as missing-lineage rather than guessed at — they were deliberately not rewritten, and draining them needs either an operator-supplied commit through the existing --commit route or a separate bounded backfill decision; (b) the taskflow close surface is still the place accumulated residue actually breaks delivery, and was deliberately not touched here; (c) an independent index oracle that marks a receipt clean after a drain, and the receipt lifecycle question of who clears a receipt whose debt is fully drained, are both still open. 2026-08-28 after slice A the remaining slices are explicitly sequenced and paused: (B) deferral release must not restore entries that were drained rather than parked, which depends on A; (C) draining automatically inside the close window is blocked pending an owner ruling on cross-card index authority, because reconciliation residue is attributed to the committing task while it blocks a different task's close, so close would have to consume another card's receipt and mutate the shared index on its behalf; (D) the 82 legacy receipts that carry retained paths without lineage remain undrainable and were deliberately not rewritten. One housekeeping item: ATM_CLOSE_WINDOW_UNRECONCILED_RESIDUE is covered by the registry's ATM_ catch-all prefix rule, exactly like its sibling ATM_CLOSE_WINDOW_FOREIGN_STAGED_TASKS which also has no exact entry, so no registry edit was required; docs/ERROR_CODES.md was deliberately NOT regenerated because `npm run generate:error-codes` rewrites source line references repository-wide and would have pulled unrelated lanes' drift into this commit. Regenerating that index is a separate housekeeping pass. 2026-08-29 read-only design review (claude-008), no code written: a measured correction to this item's own (D) strand, the confirmed mechanism behind (B), and one precision gap left by slice A. Measurement, reproducible by parsing every .atm/history/evidence/*.live-index-reconciliation.json: 88 receipts exist; 82 carry retainedPaths and those 82 name exactly ONE distinct path between them, .atm/history/evidence/git-head.jsonl, every entry with reason worktree-diverged and failure null; the 6 receipts that actually carry ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED (ATM-GOV-0315, 0331, 0352, 0353, 0355, 0385) carry ZERO retainedPaths; and the live index of this working tree currently holds 0 staged entries. Three consequences follow. (1) The "82 legacy receipts without lineage" this item described as undrainable debt are not reconciliation debt at all: git-head.jsonl is an append-only governance ledger that the commit itself appends to, so its worktree necessarily diverges from HEAD at reconciliation time and the path is retained benignly and correctly. No drain can or should advance it, and no lineage backfill would change that. (2) The 6 genuinely failed receipts name no path at all, so they are structurally undrainable by any receipt-consuming operation; whatever debt they represent was never recorded per-path. Draining legacy receipts is therefore not the open work (D) implied. (3) Because the live index is empty, the slice A residue classifier cannot fire in this repository today and neither B nor C can be exercised; they are forward-looking insurance rather than current breakage, and sequencing should reflect that. Mechanism behind B, confirmed by reading close-window-lock.ts: the close window passes the FULL unexpectedStagedFiles set, not a foreign subset, into deferForeignStagedFiles, which runs git restore --staged over it. For a residue path that call IS the drain, because it sets the index entry to HEAD. Release then restores every snapshot entry byte-for-byte unconditionally, which precisely reconstructs the debt the defer had accidentally repaired. B is therefore not a tweak to make restore skip a drained entry: at that point the code cannot even distinguish its own receipt's residue from another card's residue. Recommended split. B1 is implement-now and needs no policy: record a per-path receiptTaskId alongside each deferred entry and disclose it on release, changing no restore semantics. B1 is the mechanical gate that stops a later B2 from silently bypassing C's cross-card authority ruling, because today the data needed to make that distinction does not exist in the lock record. B2, actually skipping restoration for a proven-drained entry, should be folded into C rather than shipped alone: if C drains before the snapshot is taken, residue never enters the snapshot and B2 is eliminated by construction. C remains needs-owner-policy. Its engineering proof is already complete, since a path advances only when the current index entry equals the parent tree of its firstUnreconciledCommit AND the worktree equals HEAD; the missing piece is authority alone. The recommended shape follows the --defer-foreign-staged precedent: an explicit operator-carried opt-in such as --drain-residue, close still fail-closed by default, ordered lease publication first, then drain, then snapshot of the foreign remainder. D should be re-scoped rather than backfilled, into two disjoint populations that no longer share a remedy: P1, the 82 benign ledger retentions of .atm/history/evidence/git-head.jsonl, which are correct retentions and need only this record correction rather than any drain or backfill; and P2, the 6 historical ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED receipts (ATM-GOV-0315, 0331, 0352, 0353, 0355, 0385) that carry no retained paths at all and are therefore structurally undrainable by any receipt-consuming operation. Reconstructing lineage from reflog or history is explicitly rejected. Slice A precision gap, unfixed and reported here: diagnoseUnexpectedStaged takes classification.residueSources[0] as THE owner, so when residue spans receipts from several tasks the emitted requiredCommand names an arbitrary one; an operator following it drains part of the debt, close still blocks, and the message does not change. The fix is to emit one drain command per distinct receiptTaskId. Coupling to release work: A, B1 and C are all packages/cli/src source-only and can be written while npm packaging work is in flight, but none of them take effect until the frozen runner is rebuilt, so runner-sync must wait for that release to succeed; since B and C cannot fire today, the cost of waiting is zero. The smallest next change is this record correction itself, which is zero code, followed by B1.
containment: Quickfix on 2026-08-27 (claude-008) repaired the two seams that made a transient collision terminal and made the resulting debt unreadable. `live-index-lock-retry.ts` recognises `.git/index.lock` contention narrowly and yields the irreducible write window for a bounded, configurable number of attempts (ATM_LIVE_INDEX_LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS / ATM_LIVE_INDEX_LOCK_RETRY_DELAY_MS); the retry is safe only because the guarded write is an update-index against an already-computed HEAD entry and therefore idempotent. Reconciliation no longer aborts on the first locked path: an exhausted retry retains that single path with the new `index-locked` reason and the loop continues, so a receipt now names every committed path still behind HEAD instead of collapsing the batch into one opaque failure. The established ATM_LIVE_INDEX_RECONCILIATION_FAILED code is preserved whenever any path is left locked, so nothing downstream can read an unreconciled index as merely retained. No foreign lock is ever removed and no unbounded wait was introduced. Deterministic coverage in live-index-lock-contention.test.ts: narrow contention detection, no-contention baseline, lock released inside the retry window, lock never released across two paths, and idempotent draining on a repeat run. 2026-08-28 second quickfix (claude-008) closed the drain gap the first one left. Three seams: (1) each retained path on the receipt now carries firstUnreconciledCommit, pinned to the FIRST commit that left it behind and preserved across later blocked commits, because once a second commit rewrites a still-unreconciled path no single commit's parent-and-tree pair describes the live index any more; lineage is merged before the byte-stability comparison so re-stamping never rewrites a receipt on its own. (2) drainLiveIndexReconciliationReceipt in live-index-drain.ts is the public, idempotent operation: it reads only the receipt, proves each path against the parent tree of its recorded first-unreconciled commit AND against HEAD in the worktree, advances proven paths with one short update-index write each (through the index-lock retry), recognises previously drained paths as alreadyAligned so a repeat run is a no-op, and retains everything else untouched with a reason. It is reachable as `node atm.mjs git reconcile-live-index --task <id> [--write]`, beside the existing --commit route. (3) recoverLiveIndexAfterSuccessfulCommit no longer reports clean while unprovenPaths is non-empty — a recovery that proved nothing was reporting success, which is how accumulated debt stayed invisible. Deterministic coverage in live-index-drain.test.ts, written red first: receipt self-addressing, byte-stable lineage across repeated blocked commits, the commit-scoped recovery refusing accumulated debt without claiming clean, drain applying and then being idempotent, and refusal on a diverged worktree with a foreign staged entry left byte-identical. 2026-08-28 slice A (claude-008), diagnosis only. Read-only inventory first established two corrections to this item's own record: the close path defers staged entries with `git restore --staged`, not `git restore --worktree` (the --worktree call belongs to --defer-governance-dirty and is narrowly limited by isDeferrableGovernanceDirtyFile to git-head.jsonl and <task>.bundle-manifest.json, each snapshotted with a sha256 before restore); and residue does not only appear as staged deletions, because `git diff --cached` compares HEAD to the index, so a path HEAD deleted reads as an addition and a path HEAD added reads as a deletion. The measured defect: evaluateCloseWindowStagedIndexAdmission blocked on a class-agnostic count of unexpected staged files, so this repository's own unreconciled commits were reported as foreign staged work and the operator was told to defer — which parks a byte-exact snapshot and restores it on release, recreating the debt. inspectGitIndexOwnership already classified such paths as ordinary-unowned rather than foreign-active-owned; the admission simply did not consult any class. The repair adds close-window-residue-classification.ts, which proves residue with a dry-run drain (no index write), and a distinct ATM_CLOSE_WINDOW_UNRECONCILED_RESIDUE code whose summary and requiredCommand name the drain instead of the defer. Scope held to diagnosis: no index mutation, no change to the close-window lease publication order, and no change to what deferral parks or restores. Mixed sets keep the foreign code and the defer route because a genuine foreign entry still needs deferring; an unclassified legacy caller keeps the original wording byte-for-byte; an unreadable receipt leaves the stricter foreign treatment in place, so the classifier can only ever narrow a block, never excuse one. Coverage in tests/cli/close-window-residue-diagnosis.test.ts, with the pre-existing taskflow-close-window-lock, close-window-staged-index-disclosure, and taskflow-close-atomicity regressions confirming foreign defer/restore byte-identity is unchanged. 2026-08-29 slice B1 (claude-008), per-path residue ownership disclosure. Two seams, neither of which changes a verdict. (1) The close-window lock record now carries provenResidueEntries, one entry per staged path that a dry-run drain proved is recorded reconciliation debt, each naming the receipt task that proved it. Until now the window could not express whose debt a staged path was, so the cross-card authority question slice C must answer could not even be stated in code, let alone gated: recording the owner per path is the mechanical precondition that stops a later change from skipping restoration for a path belonging to another card without that decision being made. Disclosure only — what deferral parks and what release restores are byte-for-byte unchanged, the lease publication order is unchanged, and no index write was added. A lock written before this field exists reads back as an empty set rather than an absent field, so every consumer sees one shape. (2) residueDrainCommands emits one drain per distinct receipt owner instead of naming residueSources[0]. The former behaviour told an operator to run a command that clears part of the debt; the close then blocked again with an identical message, so a correct instruction read as a failed one. A single-owner set produces the previous recovery string byte-for-byte, so nothing regresses for the common case. Coverage: tests/cli/close-window-residue-diagnosis.test.ts gains multi-owner deduplication and ordering, the disclosure shape, single-owner byte-identity, the empty case, and the multi-owner recovery reaching the operator through the admission summary; taskflow-close-window-lock.test.ts asserts the lock record and report carry the disclosure through a real deferral and that a legacy record normalises to an empty set, alongside the pre-existing foreign defer/restore byte-identity assertions. Two adjacent suites, tests/cli/git-index-close-isolation.test.ts and tests/cli/taskflow-close-defer-governance-dirty.test.ts, fail identically before and after this change (verified by running them against the HEAD copies of the touched sources) and are pre-existing, unrelated failures.
